acquisition method: Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) was performed with the resolution of the Orbitrap set to 35,000
alkylation reagent: Reduced cysteines were alkylated with 20 mM 2-chloroacetamide diluted in HEPES
alkylation concentration: Reduced cysteines were alkylated with 20 mM 2-chloroacetamide diluted in HEPES
cleavage agent: Digestion of samples was done with trypsin, in an enzyme to protein ratio 1:50 overnight at 37°C.
collision energy: The normalized collision energy of 32 was applied
enrichment method: performed a co-immunoprecipitation with rat hippocampus samples followed by TMT/MS.
fractionation method: Offline high pH reverse phase fractionation
Offline high pH reverse phase fractionation was carried out on an Agilent 1200 Infinity high-performance liquid chromatography system
instrument: The outlet of the analytical column was coupled directly to a QExactive plus (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) mass spectrometer
ionization type: coupled directly to a QExactive plus (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA) mass spectrometer using the Proxeon nano-flow source in positive ion mode.
labeling: Peptides were labeled with TMT10plex Isobaric Label Reagent (ThermoFisher)
mass analyzer: Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) was performed with the resolution of the Orbitrap set to 35,000
precursor tolerance: For the full scan (MS1), a mass error tolerance of 10 ppm
fragment tolerance: and for MS/MS (MS2) spectra of 0.02 Da was set.
ptm: Carbamidomethyl (C) fixed; TMT10 (K) fixed; Acetyl (Protein N-term) variable; Oxidation (M) variable; TMT10 (N-term) variable

The following modifications were included in the search parameters: Carbamidomethyl (C) and TMT10 (K; fixed modification), Acetyl (Protein N-term), Oxidation (M) and TMT10 (N-term; variable modifications).
reduction reagent: The reduction of disulfide bridges in cysteine-containing proteins was performed with 10 mM DTT
reduction concentration: The reduction of disulfide bridges in cysteine-containing proteins was performed with 10 mM DTT
